What Should the New Congress Do?
More from our inbox:
This is the second of two rounds of letters in response to an Opinion article about ideas for the new Democratic-controlled Congress. The first round was published on Thursday.
To the Editor:
Re “8 Big Ideas for the Next Congress” (Opinion, Nov. 8):
You listed eight things the new Congress should do, and each is worthy. Let me add a ninth: Congress should work with the states to create local citizens’ assemblies that decide how we want to benefit from artificial intelligence and how to avoid its many dangers.
These assemblies would be made up of ordinary citizens chosen at random. They would be nonpartisan and free from political pressure. Members would hear from experts, question them, deliberate with one another and make recommendations.
This idea is neither new nor utopian. For nearly two centuries, Athenian democracy chose its governing council, its juries and most public officials by lottery. In our own time, Ireland has used assemblies made up mostly of randomly selected citizens to take up same-sex marriage and abortion, questions politicians had avoided for decades. Voters approved the referendums that followed.
An issue as fundamental as A.I. should not be left in the hands of a few billionaires, or even of politicians. It belongs to all of us.
The political scientist Hélène Landemore’s new book, “Politics Without Politicians: The Case for Citizen Rule,” is a good primer on how this could work.
